questions.q: A motor transfers 6000 J of energy in 30 s. Calculate its power.
A current of 0.50 A flows for 120 s. Calculate the charge that flows.
A potential difference of 12 V is applied across a 4.0 ohm resistor. Calculate the current.
questions.explain: Rearranging V = I R gives I = V / R = 12 / 4.0 = 3 A.

questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explain: A vector has both magnitude and direction. Velocity has direction, so it is a vector; mass, temperature and speed are scalars (magnitude only).

questions.q: A 2000 W kettle is switched on for 90 s. Calculate the energy transferred.
questions.explain: Rearranging P = E / t gives E = P t = 2000 x 90 = 180 000 J.

questions.q: A charge of 90 C flows through a wire in 30 s. Calculate the current.
questions.explain: Rearranging Q = I t gives I = Q / t = 90 / 30 = 3 A.

questions.q: A current of 0.25 A flows through a resistor when 5.0 V is applied across it. Calculate its resistance.
questions.explain: Rearranging V = I R gives R = V / I = 5.0 / 0.25 = 20 ohm.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between energy and power?
options: Power is energy stored; energy is the rate of transfer
Energy is measured in watts; power in joules
Power is the rate at which energy is transferred
Energy and power are the same quantity
questions.explain: Power is the energy transferred per second (P = E/t), measured in watts; energy is measured in joules. Confusing the two is a common error.

questions.q: A student says 'current is used up as it goes round a series circuit, so the second lamp is dimmer.' Why is this wrong?
options: Current is the same everywhere in a series circuit
Current increases round a series circuit
Current is only in the first half of the circuit
Current is voltage divided by charge
questions.explain: Current is the rate of flow of charge and is the same at every point in a single series loop. Charge (and current) is not 'used up'; energy is transferred from the potential difference.

questions.q: Which of these is the correct SI base unit of mass?
questions.explain: The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg). The gram is a smaller unit, the newton is the unit of force, and the pound is not an SI unit.

questions.q: Which quantity is measured in a derived unit rather than an SI base unit?
questions.explain: A derived unit is built from base units. Speed (m/s) is metres divided by seconds, so it is derived. The second, metre and kilogram are SI base units.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of electric current?
questions.explain: Current is an SI base quantity and its base unit is the ampere (A). The coulomb (charge), volt (p.d.) and ohm (resistance) are derived units.

questions.q: To find the time t in the equation P = E / t, which rearrangement is correct?
questions.explain: Starting from P = E/t, multiply both sides by t then divide by P: t = E / P. A common error is to write t = P/E by inverting the wrong way.

questions.q: Using P = E / t, a device transfers 4500 J of energy with a power of 150 W. Calculate the time taken.
questions.explain: Rearranging P = E/t gives t = E/P = 4500 / 150 = 30 s.

questions.q: Write the number 0.04736 to 2 significant figures.
questions.explain: The first significant figure is the 4, the second is the 7. The next digit is 3 (less than 5), so we round down and keep 0.047. Leading zeros are not significant.

questions.q: A calculator gives an answer of 12.6748 m/s. Written to 3 significant figures, this is:
questions.explain: The first three significant figures are 1, 2 and 6. The next digit is 7 (5 or more), so the 6 rounds up to 7, giving 12.7 m/s.

questions.q: How is the number 5 600 000 written in standard form?
questions.explain: Standard form is A × 10ⁿ where 1 ≤ A < 10. Moving the decimal point so one non-zero digit is in front of it gives 5.6, and we moved it 6 places, so 5.6 × 10⁶.

questions.q: The prefix 'kilo' (as in kilometre) means multiply by:
questions.explain: 'Kilo' means ×1000 (10³), so 1 km = 1000 m. 'Centi' means ÷100 and 'milli' means ÷1000; 'mega' means ×1 000 000.

questions.q: Which of these quantities is a scalar?
questions.explain: A scalar has magnitude only. Distance is a scalar; force, displacement and acceleration all have direction, so they are vectors. (Distance vs displacement is a common trap.)
